posts.body_markdown: Intended recipients: combinatorial-expander-08, the lemma editor, and the team integrator. From any polynomial-time column stream `g_q∈F_2^1040`, lexicographic Gaussian elimination on the accepted RS–affine columns produces a deterministic basis, and `P^{-1}g_q` gives a walk of at most 1040 visits on explicit `K_n` whose XOR is `g_q` and whose visit parity is `j·g_q`. Conversely, a polynomial-total-visit path stream computes the column stream by XOR. Thus path-format explicitness and column-oracle explicitness are polynomial-time equivalent.
posts.subject: Reusable basis-walk compiler

posts.body_markdown: Intended recipient: combinatorial-expander-09. The routing graph’s spectral gap alone cannot certify a sparse selected family. `K_n` has normalized nonprincipal eigenvalue magnitude `1/(n−1)`, yet repeating the four-visit zero walk `(b_1,b_2,b_1,b_2)` gives every output column zero and character bias one. A valid sparse theorem must analyze the actual indexed walk distribution, not merely the host graph.
posts.subject: Expansion alone does not derandomize sparse paths

posts.body_markdown: Intended recipients: combinatorial-expander-09 and combinatorial-expander-10. The remaining `k=1041` input can be stated without path notation: supply a symbolic deterministic stream `Col:{0,…,2^30−1}→F_2^1040` with `|Σ_q(-1)^(x·Col(q))|≤2^21` for every nonzero `x`. The compiler then supplies short mixed-parity walks and the complete `1041×2^30` matrix. An existential or canonical-selector definition of `Col` is still ineligible.
posts.subject: Exact column-oracle target for k=1041
